title: CoLA: Cross-Modal Low-rank Adaptation for Multimodal Downstream Tasks
claim: Prior adaptation methods tune each modality in isolation; ours adds cross-pathways so modalities exchange information during adaptation.
layout: 2 stacked panels split by dashed line; left-to-right flow, colored cross-links in ours
description: Two vertically stacked panels separated by a dashed line. Panel (a), labeled LoRA, shows two modality encoders, one green and one blue. Each encoder has rounded boxes for Layer i to Layer N or Layer j to Layer M. Each layer has a purple LoRA block with a flame icon (tunable) and a snowflake icon (frozen). Black arrows run left to right from the input bars, through the encoders, to an orange MultiModal Downstream Tasks box. Each modality is processed independently. Panel (b), labeled CoLA (Ours), has the same layout, but the purple blocks read CoLA. Added green and blue arrows cross between the encoders and feed each modality's signal into the other encoder's CoLA block. A Frozen/Tunable legend sits at the top right. The eye goes first to the crossing colored arrows in (b).
caption: Comparison of LoRA and CoLA in dual-encoder architectures for multimodal tasks. (a) LoRA applies independent low-rank adaptation within each modality without cross-modal interaction. (b) CoLA enables cross-modal interaction through inter-modal fusion pathways, allowing information exchange between Modality 1 and Modality 2 during the low-rank adaptation process. Modality 1 and Modality 2 can be vision, language, or audio. The multimodal tasks include vision-language (REC and RES) and audio-visual (AVE and AVS) downstream tasks.
abstract: Foundation models have revolutionized AI, but adapting them efficiently for multimodal tasks, particularly in dual-stream architectures composed of unimodal encoders, such as DINO and BERT, remains a significant challenge. ParameterEfficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods like LowRank Adaptation (LoRA) enable lightweight adaptation, yet they operate in isolation within each modality, limiting their ability in capturing cross-modal interactions. In this paper, we take a step in bridging this gap with Cross-Modal LowRank Adaptation (CoLA), a novel PEFT framework that extends LoRA by introducing a dedicated inter-modal adaptation pathway alongside the standard intra-modal one. This dual-path design enables CoLA to adapt unimodal foundation models to multimodal tasks effectively, without interference between modality-specific and crossmodal learning. We evaluate CoLA across a range of vision-language (RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg) and audio-visual (AVE, AVS) benchmarks, where it consistently outperforms LORA, achieving a relative gain of around 3% and 2%, respectively, while maintaining parameter efficiency. Notably, CoLA enables the first multitask PEFT framework for visual grounding, bridging a key gap in efficient multimodal adaptation. Code is available at https://github.com/peterwisu/CoLA
